name: Historical Identity Reconciliation Candidates
principles: stable instrument identity is separate from symbol namespace
current identifiers never prove historical identity by themselves
repository snapshots become PIT evidence only from their conservative availability date
day-granularity repository snapshots are usable from the following calendar day
an observed ISIN-looking value is not accepted as an ISIN unless it passes the ISIN checksum
exact ISIN equality may create a stable instrument candidate only when an explicit historical snapshot labels that value as ISIN
crypto base-token continuity is an asset-family candidate, not proof that quote pairs are the same instrument
absence never creates delisting or out-of-scope state
ambiguous symbol or ISIN mappings fail closed
candidate aliases are not strict QM-B aliases until PIT intervals and identity are verified

historical_git_history.purpose: supplement current-only symbol candidates with commit-pinned historical symbol-to-ISIN evidence without using future repository changes
